description: A sinuous, rectilinear canal–embankment complex running roughly NW–SE across the central LiDAR strip. The feature comprises a linear depression ~2–3 m wide flanked on its northeast side by a raised berm 4–6 m wide. It exhibits consistent plan curvature (concave cross–section) and slopes under 2°, typical of engineered drainage channels in other Acre interfluves.

A cluster of low rectangular platforms (raised fields) located at the eastern end of the LiDAR swath. Each platform measures approximately 40 × 60 m and stands 0.5–1.0 m above the surrounding terrain. The platforms are arranged on a gentle slope (<1.5°) with small connecting ditches visible in the DTM and faint ‘dark earth’ signatures in the co–registered NIR.

A straight, narrow causeway trending E–W in the western third of the dataset. It is 3–4 m wide, with slightly elevated shoulders and a flat top. The feature casts a distinct ridge–and–furrow hillshade signature and corresponds to a linear NIR moisture anomaly (lower reflectance) in the Sentinel-2 band 8 image.
